candidates: When a function modifies a mutable argument (e.g., a `dict`) in-place, make a defensive copy (e.g., `copy.deepcopy`) before mutating it. This is especially important in serialization/deserialization code paths (such as `dict2constraint` and similar encode/decode helpers), where the same object may be referenced elsewhere and unexpected in-place mutation can introduce subtle, hard-to-trace bugs.
